objections.claim: `admit`'s step 4 turns a peer-status issue into `claimed-by-peer` at admission, pre-worktree — so graft never reaches Step 5, where `build-claim acquire` transparently reclaims a genuinely-stale prior claim via `--force-with-lease`. The spec's own mitigation sentence — "Reclaiming stays with `/faff-tidy`'s sweep and `faff build-claim acquire`" — is false for the path the design introduces: on a direct autonomous graft of an issue whose previous executor crashed mid-claim, `acquire` is now unreachable, and the stale claim blocks every future admission until a human runs `/faff-tidy`. Today the direct graft path self-heals at Step 5; the spec changes that behaviour without listing it in the rule inventory, and its extension point ("a later ticket can turn a stale verdict into a `proceed`") defers the fix while shipping the regression.

objections.disposition_rationale: Became the stale-ref decision; the human ratified proceed with a warning so Step 5's acquire reclaims a stale ref.

objections.claim: The claimed-by-peer gate — the mechanical backstop that skipped 14 corpus records — becomes fail-open against the party it governs. `--session-id` "identifies the caller" but nothing in the spec establishes who can write it; the default is an environment variable (`$FAFF_SESSION_ID`), set by the very agent the gate exists to constrain. Worse, the peer's `session_id` is *not a secret*: the spec's own reference context says `buildClaimStore(root).read` returns "the ref's claim, whose `owner.session_id` identifies the holder". So the bypass recipe is fully stated by the design: read the peer's claim, set `FAFF_SESSION_ID` to the holder's value, call `faff graft admit --mode autonomous`, and the spec's step 4 yields `own == true` → `proceed` on an issue a peer holds. This is exactly the FAFF-209/FAFF-218 class failure the provenance marker was built to close (an agent-spoofable gesture standing in for a trust decision), reintroduced one layer up. The spec grants authority on the strength of an input and never says who can write it — under the review rules that is an objection, not a hardening note.
objections.evidence: §3 Interface — "`--session-id` identifies the caller for the own-claim test. Default `$FAFF_SESSION_ID`"; §4.1 step 4 — "`own := ref.held AND ref.claim.owner.session_id == sessionId`"; rule-inventory row 29 "changed: the caller's own build-claim ref now counts as own work"; context `bundle.js` — the idempotent re-acquire keys on `owner.session_id`, and `buildClaimStore.read` exposes it.
objections.predicted_consequence: an agent (or a compromised/diverging run) flips `claimed-by-peer` to `proceed` on a peer-held In-Progress/In-Review issue; the double-build is only stopped downstream at graft Step 5's `acquire` (`exists` refusal) — so on issues where no live build-claim exists (the exact "In Review with no ref" case the spec itself rules `claimed-by-peer`), nothing stops the concurrent build: duplicate worktrees, duplicate PRs, and a silent false `proceed` marker written into the decision-corpus record for a gate that never actually held.
objections.disposition_rationale: The own-claim test trusts no more than build-claim acquire already does; the existing session-id weakness is filed as FAFF-1433.

objections.claim: The pseudocode reads `intake := intakeVerdict(marker, labels, mode, ...); exit := intakeExit(intake, mode, interactive)`. In `intake-provenance.js`, `mode` is the **gate** mode (`"off"` short-circuits to `gate-off`; `intakeExit` blocks only on `"block"`), not `interactive|autonomous`. Built literally, `intakeExit` can never return 3 (so the table's `blocked` row is dead) and the `off` short-circuit never fires (a gate-off config still reads the marker and can warn). The spec's own stated reason for keeping the guard — "it would fire if the two ever resolved the label differently" — is exactly the case this conflation silences, so the defence-in-depth justification does not survive its own pseudocode.
objections.evidence: section 4.1 step 6; `intake-provenance.js` `intakeVerdict(marker, labels, mode, prefix, automateName)` / `intakeExit(v, mode, interactive)` in context.

objections.disposition_rationale: The intake guard gets the intake_gate mode, not the admit --mode.

objections.claim: This ticket is pitched as a prose-to-code extraction (the FAFF-1404/1405/1406 lane), but rows 36 and 38 change what a direct autonomous graft *does*: today Step 5 would acquire a fresh ref and build a peer-status issue with no ref; under this spec it returns `claimed-by-peer` before any worktree. That is not extraction — it is a new admission rule — and its corpus-level evaluation (the replay test that would show whether the new rule reproduces or diverges from what the prose actually decided) is deliberately moved to FAFF-1434, blocked by this one. So the behaviour change ships one increment ahead of the only test that checks it against reality.
